annotations.text:
WHY THIS EXISTS (2 NOVEMBER 2026)

hub.elyir.com promises that setting the hub up is "answering a few questions", and the pretend house never shows it: /try opens on a house somebody already set up. The first-run walk in the mock (FRESH=1, PR #41) now runs the whole of first run end to end, so the pretend house could too.

Some of first run happens off the screen: the hub is plugged in, it downloads the rest of itself, its own Wi-Fi and password are on a label underneath, a bulb joins when somebody switches it on. A browser has none of these. The directions differ in how they stand in for them.

Each board is the real panel on a mock house out of its box (FRESH=1 NAMES=plain), with only what the direction adds drawn around it (board.html, app/mock/try-setup-shots.mjs).

Pick one, or something else -- describe it.

TODAY: ONE DOOR, INTO A FINISHED HOUSE

Try it has one button, Start the pretend house, and it opens on a lived-in house: eight rooms, thirty things, routines. That shows what living with the hub is like. It never shows the claim the front page leads with, that setting it up is a few questions.

EVERY DIRECTION shares the way in: a second door beside the first, Set one up from the box. On a computer it opens /try on a page of its own rather than in the site's small frame, because first run is a whole screen. At the end the visitor is in the house they just described, empty but for what the hub found; nothing is kept when they leave. What a direction decides is how the off-screen parts are stood in for.

A -- NARRATED: THE REAL SCREENS, AND THE /TRY BAR SAYS THE REST

Every screen of first run, as a household sees it, the Wi-Fi question included. The bar the pretend house already has ("A pretend house · Back to the site") becomes a narrator only where something happens off the screen: while the hub downloads ("this one takes a moment"), on the Wi-Fi ("any password joins"), and where a real house needs a hand on a bulb, with a button that does it ("Switch one on"). Everywhere else it is the plain bar.

The case for it: nothing is drawn that the product does not have; the Wi-Fi screen with its own code beside it is the hub's best moment, and it is shown; one bar, already built. The case against: the longest walk, about two minutes, and the hub's label is only a sentence.

B -- THE HUB ON THE DESK

A drawn hub beside the screen. The visitor plugs it in (the screen comes on), and when the screen asks which Wi-Fi, the label on the bottom of the hub lights: its own Wi-Fi and password, which is what a phone joins. The off-screen parts become things to do with the box.

The case for it: the most like owning one; the label and the plug, which no screen can show, are shown. The case against: a drawing of hardware we do not sell yet, which every later change to the box makes wrong; on a computer the screen is two-thirds size, and on a phone the box squeezes the panel to a strip.

C -- THE QUESTIONS ONLY

One card says the plugging in is done and lists what is left: names, a passcode, where home is and which rooms, what is in the house. Then the real screens from Welcome home, without the Wi-Fi or the drive. One more card at the end says that is all a real one asks, before the house.

The case for it: the shortest walk, the least to build, and the card is the front page's promise said as a list. The case against: it skips the parts that make the hub different from an app -- its own Wi-Fi, the code on its label, a screen that needs nothing else to start -- and tells them instead of showing them.

DECIDED 2 NOVEMBER 2026: A, NARRATED

Every screen of first run as a household sees it, the Wi-Fi question first, and the /try bar narrating only where something happens off the screen: the Wi-Fi ("any password joins"), the download after it ("this one takes a moment"), and a plug or bulb waiting for a hand, with Switch one on. The bar reads the pretend house, not the page, so it follows the house wherever the visitor goes, Add included.

Built as drawn, with three things the boards did not say. The way in is a second button under Try it's words, Set one up from the box; the lit Start the pretend house stays on the picture where the page already has it. The bulb is a plug or bulb, because the pretend house's pairing brings a plug. And the hub's own Wi-Fi code beside the question is drawn by the pretend house into the page, since a picture the panel loads directly never reaches it.

site/index.html and app/src/try.ts (?box); pinned by site/site.test.mjs and app/e2e/try.spec.ts. The out-of-the-box house is the mock's FRESH=1 (app/e2e/first-run-walk.spec.ts).
